title: The exit-code contract is stated in three documents and none of them carries the 4 that shipped
body:
`bin/devbin:118` exits **4**. The exit-code contract is stated in three live documents and every one of them still reads 0/1/2/3.

## The three sites

| document | what it says |
| --- | --- |
| `usage-rules.md` | *DO honour the exit codes: 0 ok, 1 own failure or usage error, 2 unknown or inactive, 3 resolves but not implemented.* |
| `intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE-shell.md` | *Exit codes are a contract: 0 ok, 1 the command's own failure or a usage error, 2 unknown or inactive, 3 resolves but not implemented.* |
| `intent/st/COMPLETED/ST0001/acceptance.md:70` | AC-04.14 -- *The exit-code contract holds across the surface: 0 ok, 1 die, 2 unknown command, 3 not built yet* |

A fourth statement exists in `intent/issues/CLOSED/0005/`, which is a historical record and must not be edited.

The 4 is the wrong-tree refusal shipped by `fc794aa`, and it has a good in-code rationale for not reusing 2. **The code is right; the contract is behind it.**

## The two things that make this worth filing

**`fc794aa` EDITED `usage-rules.md` AND DID NOT TOUCH ITS EXIT-CODE LINE.** The commit that introduced the fourth code changed the `dvb` line in the same file, two dozen lines from the contract it was invalidating. Proximity is not a prompt.

**THE CONTRACT IS STATED THREE TIMES, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS THREE CORRECTIONS AND NOT ONE.** Two of the three are live normative documents saying the same thing in almost the same words -- a Highlander violation in the documents that define Highlander. AC-04.14 is a closed thread's acceptance criterion and is arguably immutable history; **decide that before editing it**, because a closed thread's record and a live contract are different kinds of document and the same edit is right for one and wrong for the other.

**None of the three can go red.** `tests/unit/documentation.bats` asserts the config reference and the README surface; it does not assert the exit-code contract against the code. That is why a shipped 4 and three documents saying 0-to-3 coexisted without a single failing test.

## Suggested shape, not a decision

The durable fix is not editing three files. It is either **one live statement plus pointers**, or a test that reads the codes out of the source and asserts the prose matches -- so the next code cannot ship silently. **Both are hv's call**; devbin is paused and this is filed to be sequenced, not started.
